question.problem:
The following table shows the cooling rate of a walk-in freezer over a period of $10$ hours, starting at $9\,\text{a.m}.$

| $t\,(\text{hours})$ | $9$ | $11$ | $13$ | $15$ | $17$ | $19$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R(t)\,(\text{kilojoules/hour})$ | $5$ | $4$ | $3$ | $2$ | $4$ | $k$ |

 If the right Riemann sum approximation of the total energy removed from $9\,\text{a.m}$ to $7\,\text{p.m.}$ has a value of $40$ kilojoules, then what is the value of $k?$ 

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the curve (rate vs. time) can be approximated using the formula

$$
A≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{R(11)+R(13)+R(15)+R(17)+R(19)}})\cdot {{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{width}}.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of the rate at each point:

| $t$ | $11$ | $13$ | $15$ | $17$ | $19$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $R(t)$ | $4$ | $3$ | $2$ | $4$ | $k$ |

Now, we obtain the following approximation for the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(4+3+2+4+k)\cdot 2 \\  & =2(k+13) \\  & =2k+26\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total energy removed from $9\,\text{a.m}$ to $7\,\text{p.m}.$ Since we are given that the right Riemann sum approximation of the total energy removed is $40$ kilojoules, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2k+26 & =40 \\ 2k & =40-26 \\ k & =\frac{14}{2} \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
